Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned A.G.A. for the State as well as learned counsel for the opposite party no.2 and perused the record.

2. The present transfer application has been moved by the applicant with the prayer to transfer the S.T. No.7 of 2023 (State Vs. Suhail Khan) arising out of case crime no.150 of 2022 under sections 376, 457 IPC, Police Station Kotwali Katra, District Mirzapur from the Court of Additional Sessions Judge / F.T.C.-1st, Mirzapur to any other competent Court in the same District.

It is further submitted that since the trial court was lying vacant, no proceeding was taking place since long and when a transfer application on the same ground was moved before the District & Session Judge, Mirzapur, it was rejected vide order dated 4.1.2024 on the ground that the matter is related with crime against women and the Court of Additional Sessions Judge / F.T.C.-1st,
Mirzapur is the exclusive Court which has got jurisdiction to hear and decide such cases and the other Courts have no jurisdiction in respect of such cases.

4. The learned counsel for the opposite party no.2 though opposed the transfer application, but conceded that it is a mature trial and it was also admitted that in Criminal Misc. Bail Application No.59519 of 2022, another direction was issued by the coordinate Bench of this Court vide order dated 5.4.2023 to conclude the trial of the case within a period of four months if there is no other legal impediment and the prayer for bail made by the accused was again rejected.
5.

sentences.text: Section 408 of Cr.P.C. deals with the power of Session Judge to transfer cases and appeals from one Criminal Court to another Criminal Court in his Sessions Division.

Section 408 of Cr.P.C. reads as under ?
"408. Powers of Sessions Judge to transfer cases and appeals.

(1) Whenever it is made to appear to a Sessions Judge that an order under this sub-section is expedient for the ends of justice, he may order that any particular case be transferred from one Criminal Court to another Criminal Court in his sessions division.
(2) The Sessions Judge may act either on the report of the lower Court, or on the application of a party interested, or on his own initiative.

(3) The provisions of sub-sections (3), (4), (5), (6), (7) and (9) of Section 407 shall apply in relation to an application to the Sessions Judge for an order under sub-section (1) as they apply in relation to an application to the High Court for an order under sub-section (1) of Section 407, except that sub-section (7) of that section shall so apply as if for the words "one thousand rupees" occurring therein, the words "two hundred and fifty rupees" were substituted."
6.

A bare reading of the aforesaid provision makes it explicitly clear that order for transfer of a particular case may be passed by the Sessions Judge if it appears to him that the transfer is expedient for the ends of justice and while exercising the aforesaid power, the Sessions Judge may act either on the report of the lower Court, or on the application of a party interested, or on his own initiative.

sentences.text: It is very strange that the order of this Court passed in Criminal Misc. Bail Application No.39592 of 2023 (Suhail Khan Vs. State of U.P.) wherein a time limit for three months has been fixed by this Court to conclude the trial of the said case vide order dated 22.11.2023, has been quoted in the impugned order dated 4.1.2024 passed by the learned Sessions Judge and this fact was also well within the notice of the learned Sessions Judge that the Court where the aforesaid Session Trial is pending, is lying vacant, despite that, the transfer application was rejected by the learned Sessions Judge by the impugned order without proper application of mind.

sentences.text:
8. This Court has occasioned to go through the G.O. No. 1037 / 7 - Nyay - 2 - 2014 - 36G / 2013,
Nyay Anubhag - 2 (Adhinasth Nyayalay) Lucknow dated 01 September, 2014 whereby Fast Track Courts were established in each District in the State of Uttar Pradesh for the expeditious disposal of all the cases relating to crime against women and same are running throughout the State.

It is pertinent to mention here that the establishment of such Courts does not cause any hindrance or oust the jurisdiction of other Courts in the rank of Additional District & Sessions Judge to deal with the cases relating to crime against women and there is no Government Order or Circular issued by this Court, which empowers only the aforesaid Courts of Additional Sessions Judge / Fast Track Court as created as a result of the G.O. aforesaid, to deal with the cases relating to crime against women.
The other Courts of the rank of Additional Sessions Judge are equally empowered and have jurisdiction to deal with such matters.

The Courts of Additional Sessions Judge / Fast Track Court are not the exclusive Courts like the Courts to deal with matters under the Gangster Act, POCSO Act,
S.C./S.T. Act etc.

Since a huge increase was seen in the matters relating to crime against women,
establishment of such Courts, as mentioned above, was felt as need of the time and accordingly such Courts were established and are working, but it does not mean that the other Courts of the same rank have lost their jurisdiction to deal with such cases.
The learned Sessions Judge ought to have kept these factors into mind while dealing with the transfer application and before passing the impugned order.
Moreover, the accused in the session trial under reference is under trial and this fact was also apparent on the face of the record.
This Court deprecates such casual and lackadaisical approach of the learned Sessions Judge.
9. In view of that, it would be expedient for the ends of justice to allow the transfer application.

10. The transfer application is allowed and invoking the powers under section 4 of the Cr.P.C., it is hereby ordered that the proceedings of S.T. No.7 of 2023 (State Vs. Suhail Khan) arising out of case crime no.150 of 2022 under sections 376, 457 IPC, Police Station Kotwali Katra, District Mirzapur be transferred from the Court of Additional Sessions Judge / F.T.C.-1st, Mirzapur to the Court of Sessions Judge, Mirzapur
